answer.rationale: Hard constraint is no added delivery risk: the primary contract ends in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line is at 94% with no buffer, so switch, defer, or treating second-source as the sole action would put committed volume at risk and raise TCO via disruption. Incumbent mid-cycle refusal blocks a plain price reopen, but expiry is a new-contract point; prior renewal benchmarking and multi-year volume pricing are the only path that can pursue the 18% spend cut while keeping the stable incumbent integration. Verifying the renegotiation record because that is the load-bearing claim; whether they will move after refusing a reopen remains uncertain.
